title: Limit Simulation Method: A Pre-Empirical Framework for Stress-Testing Social Theories
abstract: This paper introduces the **Limit Simulation Method (LSM)**, a pre-empirical methodology for stress-testing social theories by forcing them to operate at extreme scale before any empirical data is collected. Unlike thought experiments, which remain conceptual, and unlike RCTs, which operate at limited scale, LSM deliberately pushes a theoretical framework to its structural limits — in this case, national implementation — in order to expose failure points that small-scale experiments cannot reveal. We describe the method, contrast it with existing approaches, and document its application to V=N/D theory, which produced seven structural failure points (Katayama & Luna, 2026). title: Elevated Signalness of IceCube GOLD Events in the Leo Core Zone: A Radio-Quiet QSO and Blazar Association Hypothesis
abstract: We report a statistically significant elevation of IceCube GOLD alert signalness in the Leo core zone (RA = 120°–150°) compared to the rest of the sky. The two GOLD events within this zone (2020-06-15, Sig = 0.828, 496 TeV; 2023-10-04, Sig = 0.842, 442 TeV) exhibit a mean signalness of 0.835, versus 0.565 for the remaining 52 events (Mann-Whitney p = 0.0186; t-test p = 0.037). Physical counterpart candidates include 4C 25.26, a radio-loud QSO from the Fourth Cambridge Radio Source Catalogue located 0.164° from the 2023-10-04 event, and Fermi 4FGL sources 4FGL J0927.2+2454 (1.79°) and 4FGL J0922.6+0434 (2.46°), both within IceCube's typical 90% credible region (~1–3°). abstract: KOKU (刻) is defined in this paper as the measured silence interval between consecutive IceCube GOLD-class neutrino events. This paper formalizes the KOKU metric and proposes it as a predictive variable for the Cosmic Synchronization Standard (CSS).

title: Statistical Evidence for Multi-Population Structure in ISP Blazars: Limitations of SED-Based Classification
abstract: We investigate the luminosity distribution of Intermediate-Synchrotron-Peak (ISP) blazars in the Fermi-LAT 4LAC-DR3 catalog (N=246, after redshift selection). After accounting for redshift-dependent effects via luminosity-bin normalization, the ISP luminosity distribution exhibits statistically significant non-Gaussianity (skewness = -0.908, Anderson-Darling p < 0.001) that persists after accounting for several commonly used physical proxies (variability index, synchrotron peak frequency ν_syn, photon spectral index), and remains after both linear and non-linear regression approaches. title: An Anomalously Variable Subpopulation of ISP Blazars Irreducible to Standard Observational Biases in the 4LAC-DR3 Catalog
abstract: We report the identification of a statistically anomalous subpopulation within intermediate-synchrotron-peak (ISP) blazars using the fourth LAT AGN catalog data release 3 (4LAC-DR3). Applying Gaussian Mixture Modeling (GMM) to 520 ISP sources (ν_syn = 10^14–10^15 Hz) using spectral index, variability index, and synchrotron peak frequency as features, we identify four distinct subgroups. Among these, a cluster of 22 sources (C3) exhibits a luminosity-corrected variability residual of +1.084 (σ = 0.444), compared to −0.105 for the remaining population (KS statistic = 0.946, p < 10^−6). title: A Complete X-ray Spectral Survey of ISP BL Lac Objects in the 4LAC-DR3 High-Confidence Catalog: Evidence for a Rare Spectral Hardening Class
abstract: We present the first complete X-ray spectral survey of all 347 Intermediate-frequency-peaked BL Lac objects (ISP BL Lacs) in the 4LAC-DR3 high-confidence catalog using archival Swift-XRT data. Of 347 targets, 242 had sufficient X-ray data for spectral analysis, yielding 220 objects classified as Class-S (spectral softening; β < 0) and 14 as Class-H (spectral hardening; β > 0). Only one object, **1WGA J0506.6-0857**, exhibits statistically significant hardening at p = 0.037 (β = 2.11, r = 0.90), marking it as the most anomalous ISP BL Lac in the catalog outside TXS 0506+056. abstract: This paper presents a personal observational record spanning 2010–2026 in which the author's precious metal transactions — conducted without knowledge of IceCube neutrino data — show temporal correlation with IceCube GOLD-class events. The author registered with Tanaka Kikinzoku (田中貴金属) in 2010, before IceCube's full deployment.
